W.notes: Strengths: a compact, readable server.mjs (325 lines). serialize() at server.mjs:129-134 orders creates and deletes; the rule checks run before the queue and the overlap check inside it (server.mjs:142-182). save() (server.mjs:136-140) updates memory only after writeFile succeeds. readBody (server.mjs:93-118) counts every byte while keeping at most 10001. Ran: npm test gave 20/20 passing. My probe passed 102/102 (concurrency, save failure, restart, routing, all rules). Defects: parseStore (server.mjs:49-65) does not check the top-level keys, so a data file {"nextId":1,"bookings":[],"junk":1} is accepted and the server starts listening, though it is not the layout this server writes (X, Y and Z exit 1). It also allows overlapping stored bookings. Tests are thin: 20 coarse tests bundle many assertions, with few edge cases on the page side (app.test.mjs is 5 tests). README is only 44 lines and short on error and exit details. The app.js `.apply` spread is old-style.

X.notes: Strengths: after the body is read, request handling is fully synchronous, including fs.writeFileSync at server.mjs:96-98. That makes requests effectively one at a time with no queue, and createStore.commit (server.mjs:258-267) saves before swapping state. Routes are a table at server.mjs:124-129 with a small route() at server.mjs:108-122. The data-file check (server.mjs:62-76) rejects extra keys, duplicate ids and overlaps. main (server.mjs:278-304) sets exitCode instead of calling exit abruptly, and gives a fixed PORT message to keep stderr to one line. Ran: npm test gave 132/132 passing (server, page, final). My probe passed 102/102. README is about 180 lines. Weaknesses: the synchronous write blocks the event loop during saves; readBody (server.mjs:218-227) never settles if the client aborts mid-body (no close handler, so the request is silently dropped); sendStatic re-reads the files on every request.

Y.notes: Strengths: server.mjs:137-146 saves atomically (write a temp file, rename it over, clean up on error), and commit (server.mjs:243-247) changes memory only after the save. server.mjs:318-335 sends every request through one global queue, so concurrency is trivially correct. server.mjs:360-363 has a clientError handler; server.mjs:301-305 logs unexpected errors to stderr on one line; server.mjs:106-116 checks the data file strictly. MSG constants are at server.mjs:25-39. Ran: npm test gave 288/288 passing across 7 well-named files (static page, page behaviour, booking rules, routes, persistence, startup). My probe passed 102/102. README is about 210 lines and thorough. Weaknesses: the temp file `<file>.<pid>.tmp` is an extra write next to the data file, and rename replaces symlinks; the global queue also serialises GETs and static files behind slow saves.

Z.notes: Strengths: server.mjs:206-226 holds the store in a repository whose commit saves first and only then swaps the state (frozen), and which runs creates and deletes one at a time, so a failed save keeps the next id. server.mjs:95-107 checks the data file strictly (exact keys, ids below nextId, unique ids, no overlaps); line 103 also requires nextId+1 to stay a safe integer, so a saved file always reloads. server.mjs:309-331 routes cleanly, with the /api/bookings/ prefix handled before the static files. server.mjs:357-358 lets the stderr write finish before exiting. app.js:33-52 has one request() returning ok, error or none, matching the spec's reply model. Ran: npm test gave 607/607 passing (fake-DOM page tests, startup, persistence, body and field rules). My probe passed 102/102, and it rejected the data file with an extra key. README is about 205 lines, detailed. Minor: fieldError (server.mjs:70-78) uses ROOMS.includes without a typeof check (harmless); there is no clientError handler; about 400 lines with some ceremony (Object.freeze everywhere).

W.notes: Own tests: 20/20 pass; broad but shallow (few rule edge cases). Data-file check too loose, server.mjs:49-65: a file with an extra top-level key ({"nextId":1,"bookings":[],"x":1}) or with overlapping bookings started normally instead of printing 'cannot read data file' and exiting 1 (confirmed by probe). server.mjs:285 echoes the raw PORT value, so a PORT containing a newline breaks the one-line rule. Otherwise passed the API/routing/concurrency/persistence/failed-save probes; serialized commit in server.mjs:128-140. README (44 lines) is brief but usable.

X.notes: Own tests: 132/132 pass (server, page app with overlapping list fetches, final checks). Passed every black-box probe. server.mjs:96-98 synchronous writeFileSync makes concurrency trivially correct but blocks the event loop during saves; route table at server.mjs:108-129 is tidy; exits cleanly via process.exitCode (server.mjs:283). server.mjs:226 body reader ignores aborted requests without settling them (harmless in probes). Fixed PORT error text avoids multi-line stderr. Good README with examples.

Y.notes: Own tests: 288/288 pass (routes, rules, persistence, startup, static page checks, fake-DOM page behaviour). Passed every black-box probe, same set as W. server.mjs:137-146 saves via temp file + rename, so a failed save never corrupts the old file; server.mjs:318-335 handles all requests one at a time (simple and correct, but slow saves hold up reads); server.mjs:360 handles clientError; HttpError makes the flow clean. Strict data-file check (server.mjs:106-116). Thorough README with status codes and data format. Slightly behind W on test depth.

Z.notes: Own tests: 607/607 pass, including fake-DOM page tests (stale list fetches, cancel/submit), concurrency and persistence. Passed every black-box probe: startup errors (bad PORT, PORT checked before the data file, empty / extra-key / overlapping / directory data file, port in use), rules 1-10 in order, BOM, invalid UTF-8, chunked 413, 415/413 on a 300KB body, byte-exact routing via raw sockets, 30 concurrent overlapping POSTs -> exactly 1 x 201 and 29 x 409, unique ids, restart keeps bookings and next id, failed save -> 500 with nothing changed and no folder created. server.mjs:206-226 queue that commits only after a successful save; server.mjs:95-107 strict data-file check (even keeps nextId+1 safe). Minor: server.mjs:349 logs 'server error: ECONNRESET' on every aborted client. README covers env vars, startup, API and data file in detail.

W.notes: Ran npm test: 142/142 pass. Probe (startup, concurrency, 413/415, routing, persistence, save failure): all pass. Strengths: one validator for both POST bodies and the data file, which is checked strictly (key set, ids below nextId, no overlaps) at server.mjs:58-84; mutations run one at a time and the store changes only after the write succeeds (server.mjs:180-193); a single HttpError path maps errors to replies (server.mjs:267-278). public/app.js:47-70 re-enables the button through an onSettle callback the moment the request settles, which matches the spec closely; stale list replies are dropped by a counter (app.js:135-141). Defects: a request with `Expect: foo` gets Node's 417 and a CONNECT request is dropped with no reply (the server never handles checkExpectation or connect); on 500 it does not log the cause anywhere (server.mjs:276). README (146 lines) is thorough: env vars, startup errors, rules, examples.

X.notes: Ran npm test: 306/306 pass across 7 test files plus a fake DOM. Probe: all pass. Strengths: error messages kept in one MSG table (server.mjs:22-36); rules 1-3 and 4-9 split into pure functions (server.mjs:73-83, 189-199); mutations serialized (server.mjs:208-218); the cause of a 500 goes to stderr, never stdout (server.mjs:301); the most complete README (218 lines, every route and the exit codes). The fail() helper exits only after the stderr write has flushed (server.mjs:100-102). Defects: same as W for `Expect: foo` (417) and CONNECT (dropped); validateFields destructures with inherited lookups (server.mjs:74), harmless for JSON.parse output; the client fills rooms with append rather than replaceChildren (public/app.js:124), fine on the first load.

Y.notes: Ran npm test: 489/489 pass across 10 test files with HTML-tree and fake-DOM helpers. Probe: all pass, and it was the only one that answered `Expect: foo` with a normal 200 (server.mjs:365) and CONNECT on a known path with 405 (server.mjs:267-276, 366). Strengths: an aborted request body is rejected rather than processed (server.mjs:153-155); every request goes through one queue (server.mjs:300-308, 333) so all orderings are consistent; a store abstraction with commit-after-write (server.mjs:310-319); a separate bind-error handler is swapped for a logging one after listen (server.mjs:367-371). Client app.js mirrors the spec closely. Defects: sortBookings builds key arrays on every comparison (server.mjs:167-175), more convoluted than needed; GETs wait behind slow writes in the shared queue; README (112 lines) is shorter than W's or X's but covers usage, env vars, data file, API and rules.

Z.notes: Ran npm test: 20/20 pass; there are few, broad tests (startup, routing, rules, concurrency, persistence, save failure, plus a small DOM test). Probe: all core checks pass (concurrency 1x201/9x409, unique ids, 413/415, BOM, routing, restart, 500 on save failure with no folder created). Defects: the whole server is top-level script state (server.mjs:112-134, 141), less modular and harder to test; readBody resolves on 'close' (server.mjs:189), so a body cut off by a client abort is still processed; `Expect: foo` gets 417 and CONNECT gets no reply; on a 200 list reply with a malformed body the client renders 'No bookings.' instead of an error (public/app.js:79); var-style client code. README is minimal (41 lines): usage, env vars, an API table and a curl example, with no listing of the validation rules or the error messages.
